name: Right wing
summary: Right-wing politics is a positional label for ideologies that treat social hierarchies and inequalities as natural, inevitable or desirable, usually joined to tradition, authority, property, religion and nation. It spans the centre-right (markets, limited welfare, law and order) to populist and national-conservative forms and, at the margin, the far right.
scope: The mainstream right of present-day Western democracies, from the Burkean conservative tradition to the neoliberal centre-right and the national-conservative right, using Burke's Reflections as the founding text and the 2024 US Republican platform as a program. It is a positional label, not a program, so issues dividing its strands are scored 0 and many answers are low-confidence inferences. The extreme right (fascism, racial supremacy) and reactionary monarchism are excluded.

sources.usedFor: Conservative attitudes to tradition, change, authority, property, markets, religion and community.

sources.title: 2024 Republican Party Platform
sources.author: Republican National Committee
sources.usedFor: Modern right-wing program on taxes, deregulation, tariffs, immigration, police, defence, energy, religion and schools.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The centre-right accepts a limited welfare state including medical care, while the US right stresses choice and competition, so adherents split.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The right favours wage-setting by markets and does not usually press for large statutory rises; the US platform is silent and stresses deregulation instead.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The right is associated with free markets and neoliberal economics, though traditionalist strands distrust doctrinaire market ideology.

public-ownership.rationale: The centre-right supports the market economy and private property over nationalisation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The right favours lower taxes; the 2024 US platform pledges to make tax cuts permanent.

unions-good.rationale: Not a defining issue for the right; the neoliberal and populist right are generally wary of unions, but some strands court workers.

property-fundamental.rationale: Burke ties liberty to inherited property and holds it to be unequal by nature; property is a core right-wing commitment.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The mainstream right favours deregulation, as in the US platform's pledge to cut regulations.

cut-welfare.rationale: The centre-right backs a limited welfare state and the US platform vows to protect Social Security, but the New Right wants small government.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker ownership of firms is a socialist aim; the right defends private ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Order and security are priorities for the right, inferred from its law-and-order emphasis; libertarian and populist strands object.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Law-and-order emphasis and social conservatism suggest opposition; the US platform stresses cartels and fentanyl.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The US platform opposes censorship of lawful speech; some European centre-right parties accept hate-speech laws.

strong-leader.rationale: The early French right wanted a strong leader for order, but modern conservatives stress constitutional limits.

state-harmful.rationale: The right values order and established authority and does not seek to abolish the state.

limit-guns.rationale: The US platform defends the right to bear arms; European right parties are more accepting of regulation.

empower-police-military.rationale: Law and order and strong defence are staples of right-wing programs; the platform promises more police and the strongest military.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Social conservatism and moral traditionalism suggest opposition, inferred rather than stated.

decide-locally.rationale: Conservatives hold that families and local communities judge their own needs better than distant officials.

rehabilitation.rationale: Law-and-order emphasis favours punishment and deterrence, inferred from the platform's focus on locking up offenders.

traditional-family.rationale: Defence of the family and 'family values' is a recurring right-wing theme and a preserved institution in conservative thought.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The right is documented as opposing same-sex marriage, framed as family values, though many centre-right parties now accept it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Opposition to abortion is a documented right-wing position, though the US platform leaves it to the states.

more-religion-public.rationale: Many right movements favour religious institutions in public life; the platform backs Bible reading and an anti-Christian-bias task force.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The right rejects egalitarian projects of redistribution by group, inferred from its stance on hierarchy and equality.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the right's emphasis on natural order and traditional family roles.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultural conservatism and nationalism are central to the right and valued as inherited bonds.

gradual-change.rationale: Burke holds that a state needs some means of change to be conserved, and conservatism prefers gradual, piecemeal reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Opposition to immigration is a feature of the populist and far right and the platform promises mass deportations and a merit-based system.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The populist and national right is Eurosceptic and the platform puts America First.

free-trade.rationale: The neoliberal right backs free trade, whereas the current US platform and national conservatives favour tariffs.

nation-first.rationale: Nationalism is a core right-wing value and the platform adopts an America First policy.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed directly; neoconservatives support intervention while nationalist and traditionalist conservatives oppose it.

open-borders.rationale: The platform commits to a border wall and deportations, and the right values national borders and identity.

limit-growth.rationale: The right favours markets and growth and is documented as more sceptical of environmental limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Right-wing opinion is documented as more sceptical of climate change, though some right governments have enacted climate policy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Conservatism's pessimistic view of human nature and suspicion of utopian schemes argue against this, inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The platform includes nuclear in expanded energy production.

revolution-justified.rationale: Burke's Reflections defended inherited order against revolution, and conservatives distrust abrupt overthrow.

experts-over-public.rationale: Traditional right favours rule by the wise, but the populist right is anti-elite and distrusts experts.

central-planning.rationale: The right favours the market economy and distrusts large-scale planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Public or worker ownership of firms conflicts with the right's support for private property.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the right's preference for tax cuts and secure private property.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Burke treats inherited property as the carrier of stability across generations, and the right favours lower taxes.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from a preference for limited welfare and work-conditional support.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The platform proposes baseline tariffs and Buy American rules, whereas the neoliberal right opposes tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from the right's preference for markets over state direction.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Burke defends large holdings as a rampart and unequal property as its nature, though small ownership is also favoured.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing money and wage labor is a communist goal opposed by the right.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not a mainstream right-wing position; inferred from support for existing institutions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Only the social Catholic and Carlist strands of the right favoured corporatist arrangements; the mainstream does not.

one-party-rule.rationale: Mainstream right parties compete in democracies; one-party rule belongs to the extreme right outside this scope.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Burke defended hereditary succession and conservatives seek to preserve monarchy where it exists.

democracy-best.rationale: Modern mainstream right accepts liberal democracy, but conservatives judge it by conditions rather than in principle.

direct-votes.rationale: The populist right favours referendums while Burkean conservatism prefers representation.

workers-councils.rationale: Workers' councils are a socialist form that the right opposes.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from the right's emphasis on national unity and order.

natural-rulers.rationale: Burke accepts a decent preeminence of birth and says government needs virtue and wisdom; hierarchy is seen as natural.

political-violence-never.rationale: The right backs state force for order while opposing revolution, so adherents are split on an absolute ban.

war-builds-character.rationale: Mainstream right does not defend this; it belongs to the extreme right.

separate-church-state.rationale: Some conservatives favour state cooperation with churches; the US right stresses religious liberty.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Reactionary and religious strands want this; the mainstream right does not.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The right supports state-provided order; private provision is a libertarian view.

military-superiority.rationale: The platform commits to the strongest, most modern military.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The far right favours an ethnically defined nation, but the mainstream right frames it culturally.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The right sees hierarchy as natural or market-driven and rejects class conflict as the driver of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Right-wing thought treats inequality as natural or beneficial; Burke says those who level never equalize.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on national sovereignty and property.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from nationalism and opposition to group redress.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The neoliberal right praises self-interest while traditionalists stress duty.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Conservatives emphasise duty, community and rights grounded in history rather than abstract claims.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed by right-wing thought as such.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred; the right defends economic development and existing civilisation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Conservatives prefer gradual change and respect for institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; libertarian and bioconservative strands split.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from distrust of abstract blueprints and valuing established authority.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Order-minded and libertarian strands of the right diverge.

restore-past-order.rationale: Conservatives weight inherited order over progress, though only the reactionary right seeks restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Conservatism is described as an epistemic standpoint wary of ideological blueprints.

direct-action.rationale: The right works through parties, elections and established institutions.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred from the right's defence of existing economic life.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A communist goal, opposed by the right.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The right defends differing rewards of market or merit and rejects distribution by need as an ultimate goal.

production-for-use.rationale: The right defends production for profit in market economies.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxian exploitation theory is rejected by the right, which sees profit as the reward of enterprise and ownership.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Opposed on principle to class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Opposed to forced collectivization and favours private property.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The right defends capitalism and rejects the Marxist theory of imperialism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Only the libertarian right holds this; the mainstream accepts taxation, favouring lower taxes.

harm-principle.rationale: Social conservatives accept restricting conduct on moral grounds.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Conservatives root rights in communities and inherited tradition rather than abstract individual claims.

conscription.rationale: Right-wing views vary; the right backs strong defence but no clear position on conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred; the right values national belonging and rooted community over exit.

state-as-business.rationale: The neoliberal right supports this, but traditional conservatives do not.

positive-liberty.rationale: The right favours freedom from interference and limited state provision, as in the US platform.

media-academia-power.rationale: A recurrent populist-right claim, not documented in my sources.

hereditarian-race.rationale: A far-right claim; the mainstream right disavows it.

organic-representation.rationale: Conservatives value families, communities and corporate bodies, and Burke emphasised the little platoon.

total-state.rationale: Directing every area of life is a far-right/fascist trait outside the mainstream right.

national-rebirth.rationale: Palingenetic nationalism belongs to the extreme right; conservatives prefer continuity.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Aggressive expansion is a far-right trait, and the mainstream right stresses defence and sovereignty.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal loyalty is a reactionary position not held by mainstream right.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is not defended by the modern right.

universal-morality.rationale: The right appeals to natural law and moral order.

single-common-good.rationale: Conservatives speak of the common good but accept plural interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The platform supports Israel, though that is a policy rather than a principle of the right.

revive-national-language.rationale: Cultural nationalism could favour it but it is not a general position.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic company control conflicts with the right's defence of ownership.

school-vouchers.rationale: The platform supports universal school choice and the neoliberal right backs vouchers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The neoliberal right stresses fiscal restraint, though the platform's tax cuts qualify this.

economic-freedom.rationale: The right ties liberty to property and markets.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not an issue the right addresses.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nationalism is a core right-wing value.

force-without-un.rationale: America First foreign policy and sovereignty ethos.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Conservatives value religion and tradition and doubt reason alone.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The right's nationalism and anti-immigration stance imply reserving benefits for citizens.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the right's emphasis on responsibility and critique of dependency.

class-collaboration.rationale: Paternalist and organic conservatism sees classes as partners with duties to each other.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred; the right backs Western alliances.

workers-nation.rationale: Marxist international class organisation is rejected, and nationalist labour appeals are a minority.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Social conservatives favour this but modern centre-right parties do not.

ban-interest.rationale: The right defends credit and finance within markets.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: This belongs to the extreme right and outside the mainstream.

state-class-instrument.rationale: This is a Marxist view rejected by the right.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The platform commits to expanded drilling and lifting limits on oil, gas and coal.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The right frames immigration around national culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: A far-right and some populist claim; the mainstream right does not endorse it.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not a defining issue of the right.

national-mission.rationale: Neoconservatives favour promoting democracy abroad while national conservatives reject it, so the right is split.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The right generally accepts natural hierarchies and denies that society is organised to disadvantage women.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Populist strands say yes while establishment conservatives defend political institutions, so adherents are split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy was once supported by some on the right, but the mainstream today opposes it, often on religious grounds; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The mainstream right backs police and military and is wary of prosecuting past conduct; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Libertarian and market strands agree but conservatives and national conservatives want a wider state role, so it is split.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The mainstream right does not endorse discouraging mixed marriage, though traditionalists stress community and kinship; inferred, with the extreme right excluded.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The right sees hierarchies as natural but the mainstream accepts equal rights before the law; as moral worth is also read differently by strands, adherents split.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The right opposes socialism but the statement concerns revolutionary strategy, which the right does not address.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The mainstream right tends to defend national origins and Western settler states against the colonial label; inferred from its nationalism.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The right is split between universal equality before the law and respect for religious and traditional communities.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The right's close ties to religion make it hostile to legal limits on conversion, which the platform defends as religious liberty; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A regional issue on which the right has no shared position.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The right favours a public place for religion, and the platform backs school prayer and religious expression in schools; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine that the right does not address.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Burke rejected a pure consent theory in favour of prescription and tradition, while the platform invokes government by the people; adherents split.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The right usually holds that truth and expertise are discoverable and rejects power-based accounts of knowledge as relativist; inferred, with populist exceptions.

trade-surplus.rationale: The market-oriented centre-right favours free trade while national-conservatives and the 2024 platform favour tariffs; adherents split.

population-transfer.rationale: The mainstream right opposes forced expulsion of citizens or minorities, as the extreme right is excluded, though it backs deporting unlawful migrants; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The right accepts force for law, order, defence and security, and its libertarian wing alone holds an absolute ban; inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The right treats inequality and hierarchy as natural and favours markets and merit-based rivalry over levelling.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Right-wing adherents split between defending free political competition and banning anti-constitutional parties; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The right stresses negative liberty and property rights and treats unused power as acceptable if constrained by law and custom; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Burke defended a balanced constitution with checks among King, Lords and Commons, and the American right defends constitutional separation of powers.

vanguard-party.rationale: The right rejects revolutionary class politics and leading parties; inferred from Burke's hostility to revolutionary clubs.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The right holds that laws should treat all alike and that social hierarchies are natural, not rank groups by need.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right emphasis on property ownership and market-oriented housing policy; not a defined program of the label.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right preference for market flexibility and law and order; strands differ on how far to go.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream right locates poverty in incentives and institutions rather than population, though a Malthusian minority exists.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: National-conservative strands say yes while centre-right and market-liberal strands deny it, so adherents are split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Burke defends a natural aristocracy and tested institutions, and rejects offices open to anyone by equal right or chance.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Law-and-order strands favor emergency powers, while constitutionalist conservatives resist suspending legal protections; adherents are split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Market-oriented right opposes price ceilings as a distortion of free exchange; inferred from its economic principles.

party-controls-media.rationale: The mainstream right defends press and online speech against government control; the platform stresses free speech.

party-commands-army.rationale: Mainstream right stands for constitutional civilian command of the military, not command by a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from the right's stress on national membership, tradition and integration before citizenship.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream right accepts pay that attracts talent and rejects levelling, though populist strands criticise elite privilege.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred: the Burkean tradition says representatives owe judgment, not obedience, while parliamentary right parties enforce whips, so the strands split.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred: the national-conservative and US right stress sovereignty and the 2024 platform is sceptical of international bodies, but the centre-right in Europe supports the EU.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred: the US right favours a strong commander in chief while parliamentary conservatives accept legislative control, so adherents split.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Inferred: Anglican and Catholic conservatives value episcopal order, but the US right is mostly Protestant and congregational, so it is split.

clerical-rule.rationale: Inferred: the right values religion in public life, but the 2024 platform stresses religious liberty rather than clergy holding authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The right stresses nation, loyalty and defence, so working for one's own government's defeat is contrary to its view.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred: traditionalist conservatives support moral limits on art, while the liberal and libertarian right defends free expression.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred: the US right has defended term limits for presidents, but some national-conservatives favour leaving the choice to voters, so it is split.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred: populist and US state-level right movements have used recall, while the Burkean tradition favours stable terms and representative judgment.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Inferred from the Republican platform's "peace through strength" and America First stress; the wider right is split between Atlanticist and nationalist views.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Private property is central to the right (Burke, SEP), so a ban on renting out property would be rejected.

people-in-arms.rationale: The right backs gun rights but also a strong professional military; replacing the army with an armed citizenry is inferred as rejected.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred from conservative attachment to land, community and tradition, which it contrasts with urban rootlessness.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The right has no single position on reunification; national-conservatives may favour it but others value existing borders and stability.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred from the modern right's populist criticism of academic and cultural elites; Burke's natural aristocracy is not an academic one.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred from conservative defence of the inherited culture of one's own civilization, though many on the right accept pluralism.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from the law-and-order emphasis of the mainstream right, which generally backs capital punishment for the gravest crimes; some libertarian and religious conservatives dissent.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the platform's stress on parental rights and opposition to gender ideology in schools.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Adherents are split: religious conservatives favour it, while many centre-right and neoliberal supporters defend science-only teaching.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the conservative concern for public morality and tradition; libertarian strands dissent.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from the national-conservative emphasis on border control and a bounded national community, which favours restricting birthright citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from the right's preference for a common national language and cultural unity.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred from the platform's emphasis on religious liberty, though the right is less sympathetic to non-Christian minorities.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Burke defends prescription and custom, so the right values shared custom over encouraging eccentricity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from the right's respect for contracts and property, which treats debts as obligations to be honoured.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Strands differ: national conservatives stress sovereignty, while market conservatives favour open economies; adherents are split.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Burke prefers inherited, gradual constitutional change over remaking a constitution from scratch.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Right strands differ: authoritarian strands accept it while liberal-conservatives defend liberties; adherents are split.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from the priority on duties to compatriots and nation; the Republican platform stresses 'America First'.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from the Republican platform's emphasis on strong national defence and sovereignty.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The right is split: some back direct election of the president, while parliamentary and monarchist conservatives do not.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right's emphasis on sound money and price stability.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Right strands differ on territorial compromise; the label takes no side.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Burke and the Republican platform defend property rights, so the right resists making ownership conditional on the community's judgement.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The right is anti-communist but the question is not one the label addresses.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from the right's general preference for market solutions and scepticism of regulation before harm is proven; the Republican platform opposes costly climate regulation.

collective-defense.rationale: The mainstream right treats alliances such as NATO as core to security, though its populist wing questions the cost.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream right's support for national sovereignty and the existing order of states; adherents differ over particular cases.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The right defends religion and the independence of churches; the Republican platform stresses religious liberty.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from the Burkean tradition of monarchy and a unifying head of state; US-style partisan presidents are accepted too.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the right's emphasis on national unity and state authority; libertarian-leaning strands accept secession.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The right is split between states' rights and decentralisation advocates and those who prefer a uniform national order.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The right values monarchy and religion, but the mainstream right in democracies no longer holds rulers divine; only reactionary strands do.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Many centre-right and market-oriented parties favour flatter taxes and lower top rates, but not all adherents back a strictly flat rate.

character-from-environment.rationale: Right-wing thought accepts natural hierarchies and inherited differences, as Burke and later conservatives did, though it also stresses upbringing and moral formation.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Conservatism holds that rulers are bound by law and prescription; Burke defended constitutional limits on power.

space-expansion.rationale: Not a defining right-wing issue; the Republican platform backs space programs, while fiscal conservatives resist the cost.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Burke praised the mixture of crown, lords and commons as the English constitution, and conservatives value balanced government.

leader-cult.rationale: The mainstream right in democracies honours leaders but does not usually endorse mass cults of personality; populist strands come close.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred: the right's fathers' rights and traditional-family strands pull in different directions on equal-time presumptions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The right rejects Marxist class struggle and Burke condemns levelling, so a call to continue class war under socialism runs against its core.

land-redistribution.rationale: Conservatives defend established property and Burke attacks seizing estates, so expropriating landowners is rejected.

refugee-return.rationale: Right-wing strands differ on this; it is not a defining right-wing issue.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream right's respect for existing states and borders; irredentism is confined to the far right, which the scope excludes.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The mainstream right defends religion in public life but, in the scope of Western democracies, not legal punishment of leaving it; inferred from the platform's stress on religious liberty.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from the Western right's stress on individual liberty and religious freedom, though some traditionalists favour modesty norms.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from the right's emphasis on national sovereignty, though the neoliberal centre-right often accepts monetary union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from the right's attachment to existing nations and borders over cross-border political unions.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the national-conservative and mainstream preference for a common national culture and institutions over separate minority ones.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: This is not a defining right-wing question and the strands differ on minority rights and national belonging.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Conservatives stress tradition, religion and inherited ideas as what shape societies, in contrast to Marxist materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: The neoliberal right favours antitrust enforcement for competition while others tolerate large firms, so adherents split.

no-bailouts.rationale: Free-market conservatives oppose bailouts while others on the right have backed rescues of key firms, so adherents split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Burke distrusted unchecked popular majorities, though the populist right resists judicial constraint; inferred and contested.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The right generally prefers merit and voters to quotas; inferred, and the platform opposes preferences by group.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The centre-right favours trade, though the national-conservative strand backs tariffs; a bloc closed to outside trade goes beyond both.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from the right's preference for trade deals focused on trade and for deregulation over binding standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: The right defends property and reward for effort, and Burke accepts unequal rewards, so it rejects replacing pay with duty as the main spur.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Burke condemns revolution and the right prizes order and authority, so a small armed group making a revolution is rejected.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Burke defends inherited rank and a natural aristocracy, and many on the right keep monarchy and tradition, though modern strands accept abolition.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The mainstream right stresses national heritage and tradition in education, and the Republican platform backs teaching that centres American history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred: the modern mainstream right does not defend colonial rule, though a minority still speaks of civilizational mission.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Republican platform calls for patriotic education that builds pride in the nation and its symbols, and the conservative tradition values national attachment.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The Republican platform opposes racial preferences and demands race-neutral admissions and hiring.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred: the right favours sound money and independent central banking over state-directed money creation, though some strands distrust the banks.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred: the right defends capitalism as resilient and self-correcting through markets and growth.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Adherents split between a nationalist right that values influence abroad and a restraint-minded right that does not.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred: the right favours trade and investment, though the national-conservative strand backs tariffs and economic nationalism for the rich countries themselves.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: the right rejects class-exploitation theory and the idea that domestic workers are an exploited class.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian-leaning adherents defend property and association rights, while the mainstream right accepts civil rights law, so adherents split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Republican platform defends the Constitution and its guarantees of rights against majorities and government, in line with the right's attachment to settled institutions.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from prescription and respect for inherited arrangements; the right generally holds that settled borders and treaties stand.

elective-rulers.rationale: Burke defended hereditary monarchy while the US and other republican rights accept elected heads of state; split.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: the conservative tradition accepts majority decisions within constitutional forms and does not give members a veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Burke allowed resistance only in extreme necessity and stressed obedience, while others on the right differ; split.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The British-Burkean right backs parliament but the US right relies on courts and the executive; split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred: the right broadly accepts that animal cruelty is wrong, but it is not a defining issue.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: the right accepts farming and research with limits on cruelty.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Burke's natural aristocracy and conservative paternalism imply duties of the privileged, though not stated as a rule; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred from the right's stress on duty, nation and public order, which leaves little room for withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The right does not usually see mass culture as an instrument of control; the idea belongs to Marxist critique.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The right tends to explain power by interests, tradition and law, not by manufactured consent.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The right supports markets and trade; the 2024 platform treats tariffs and trade as American strength, not an exploitation structure.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred: the national-conservative right might favour it, but the mainstream accepts equal rights for naturalized citizens.

party-own-road.rationale: The right has no stake in how communist parties relate to one another.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from the right's preference for markets and national independence; the 2024 platform stresses American self-reliance.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from the right's respect for settled arrangements and order, though national-conservatives may differ.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream right holds equal citizenship and rejects rule by ancestry.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The right opposes fascism but is split on making antifascism a founding value of the constitution.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anti-communism is a long-standing right-wing theme, and many on the right condemn both as totalitarian.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Most mainstream right voices accept slavery as the war's cause, though some in the US right argue states' rights; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from respect for tradition and heritage (Burke, conservatism), which favours preserving monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from the right's stress on traditional family and opposition to preferential programmes focused on women.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred: the right is more receptive to claims of male victimhood and equal protection for abused men.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: National-conservatives and cultural relativists agree, while neoconservatives and liberal-minded right hold democracy to be universal; split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The mainstream right backs the military and order but holds that civilians control it; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: The right treats care at home as a family duty and opposes paying it as labour from public funds.

filial-duty.rationale: Conservatives treat the family and inherited obligations across generations as foundations of social order; Burke's 'little platoons' idea.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream right values elected government and established hierarchy more than rule by examination; this is not a defining right-wing issue.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The 2024 Republican platform stresses protecting strategic industries from foreign adversaries, though free-market right strands disagree.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Social conservatives oppose easy divorce while libertarian and centre-right strands accept it, so adherents are split.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Burke's speech to the electors of Bristol argues that a representative owes his judgment, not obedience to instructions, which is the classic conservative position.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The market right favours private accounts but the mainstream Republican program defends existing Social Security, so strands are split.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Burke defends secure private property and inheritance of estates as pillars of order; the right rejects communal use-only tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Burke defends the legislature's constitutional control over supply as part of the balanced constitution; the right broadly accepts it.

single-official-language.rationale: The national-conservative right commonly backs a common national language such as English, but other strands do not press the point.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The 2024 Republican platform criticises foreign adversaries buying US farmland; inferred as a mainstream right position.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The 2024 platform opposes race-conscious equity policies; the right generally holds that discrimination means intentional unequal treatment.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Market-oriented right strands defend consumer choice, though traditionalists criticise materialism; inferred as mild disagreement.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Cold War right backed anti-communist insurgents while the newer restraint-minded right opposes it, so adherents are split.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream Western right treats alliances as voluntary and does not defend forced intervention against allies.

corporate-influence.rationale: Right-wing adherents mostly see business lobbying as ordinary politics and favor limits on government over limits on corporate speech; populist strands disagree. Inferred from the pro-property, pro-market outlook.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The national-sovereignty emphasis of the contemporary right supports screening foreign money in civil society. Inferred from the program's stress on sovereignty.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Support for the family and for national continuity leads the right to favor pro-family incentives over immigration to offset decline; centre-right strands are less committed. Inferred from its family emphasis.

residents-only-property.rationale: The right defends property rights and free purchase, so local limits on who may buy are usually opposed, though rural conservatives sometimes favor them. Inferred from its property principles.

job-guarantee.rationale: The right holds that jobs come from the private market and resists an open-ended state employer. Inferred from its market and limited-state outlook.

democratic-peace.rationale: Neoconservatives promote democracy abroad, while realists and national conservatives reject it as a path to peace, so adherents split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Burkean conservatism and the law-and-order right hold that law commands obedience as part of an inherited order, not only when individuals judge it just.

non-intervention.rationale: Most of the mainstream right accepts intervention in some cases, such as atrocities or security threats, so it rejects an absolute ban. Inferred from the platform's security stance.

industrial-unions.rationale: The right generally prefers craft, enterprise or company-based bargaining to class-wide industrial unions. Inferred from its stance on organized labor.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The mainstream right scoped here rejects conspiracy theories about minorities; they belong to the excluded extreme right. Inferred from that scope.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage as a legally recognized institution is central to the right's support for the family and tradition.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The right accepts openness of government records as a check on state power, with exemptions for security. Inferred from its limited-government principles.

local-production.rationale: Free-market strands favor efficient trade while national and agrarian conservatives favor local and domestic production, so adherents split.

informal-organisation.rationale: The right values established institutions, parties and hierarchies over loose informal groups. Inferred from its respect for order and institutions.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The contemporary right defends national sovereignty and constitutional supremacy against international bodies.

religious-nation.rationale: The religious right ties the nation to its faith, while the secular and civic centre-right does not, so adherents split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from the right's emphasis on national sovereignty and equal standing of nation-states; ritual tribute is foreign to it.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Strands differ: neoliberals favour fiscal competition while national conservatives defend national solidarity, so adherents split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The right defends private property, and Burke defended unequal property against levelling; common ownership of the means of production is the socialist position it opposes.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anti-communism was a defining plank of the Cold War right and persists, though modern strands differ on how far to confront it; inferred from that history.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The centre-right favours choice and private providers inside publicly funded services; the 2024 platform backs school choice. Traditionalist strands care less.

religion-illusion.rationale: Conservative thought values religion as a pillar of social order, and Burke defended religious establishment, so it rejects reading religion as consolation that fades.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Market-oriented strands praise capitalism's creation of wealth, while traditionalists distrust its effects on community, so this is inferred and contested.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the right's preference for reform within existing institutions and markets rather than economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Conservatism treats the family as a basic institution of social order and prefers private family arrangements to public substitutes.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Mainstream right favours continuity of language, but official purges of loanwords are a fringe nationalist policy; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Burke's respect for prescription and inherited arrangements favours honouring treaties, but national-conservatives stress sovereign discretion, so adherents split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from the right's defence of private property and existing institutions; communal ownership contradicts both.

majority-settlement.rationale: The mainstream right does not promote majority settlement of minority regions; only the nationalist margin does. Inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The mainstream right is committed to capitalism or its reformed forms, so it rejects a third course; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Mainstream right strands split: national conservatives stress historical ties, while liberal-minded centre-right voices do not.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial is associated with the extreme right, which the scope excludes; the mainstream right rejects it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The mainstream right has largely accepted decriminalisation, and the 2024 platform does not call for criminal penalties, though religious conservatives dissent.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The right prizes order but within the rule of law, and the 2024 platform stresses free speech and opposes government censorship.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Burke defends an established church, but the modern right defends religious liberty rather than punishment of blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from the modern right's rejection of empire for gain; the scoped right is not colonial.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The mainstream Western right has no settled view on this Islamic doctrine; it falls outside the scope.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from the right's emphasis on legitimate order and rule of law over rebellion; Burke condemns revolutions against established governments.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Burke defends representation by chosen deputies over direct popular decision-making, and the right is wary of such experiments.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The 2024 platform opposes identity-based doctrines and critical race theory in favour of equal treatment of individuals.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The 2024 platform opposes gender-identity policies, for example in women's sports and schools.

assisted-dying.rationale: Religious and traditional conservatives oppose it, though some libertarian-leaning right voices differ.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The right defends the left-right division and its own side; the claim is typical of centrist positions.

alienated-labor.rationale: The right defends private property and wage labour and rejects the Marxist concept of alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Right-wing opinion is split on Islam: some voices stress culture and immigration, others religious liberty.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Burke ties the state to religion and divine order, but modern right strands are split on whether authority derives from God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The platform defends religious liberty and expression in public life, so bans on religious dress run against it.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Adherents differ between business-friendly deregulation and calls to curb abuses.

social-market-economy.rationale: The right splits between Christian-democratic and free-market strands, so the middle path is contested.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The right stresses military strength and national defence; the 2024 platform champions peace through strength.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the right's market emphasis that unequal growth lifts others over time; adherents differ in degree.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The right splits between alliance-minded Atlanticists and America First non-interventionists.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Burke defended hereditary succession, but the modern right mostly accepts elected heads of state, so adherents split.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The centre-right favours profit-making private banking and free enterprise, inferred from its market orientation.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Fiscal discipline leads the centre-right to accept lender conditions, while national-conservatives resist outside dictation; adherents split.

property-franchise.rationale: Burke tied representation to property, but today's right backs universal adult suffrage, inferred from the Republican platform's emphasis on voting by citizens.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The right treats gender roles and use of nature as largely natural or legitimate, so this linked critique is not accepted, inferred from its defence of hierarchy.

reification.rationale: This is a Marxist claim about capitalism; the right defends markets and property and would reject it, inferred from its principles.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The right defends property rights and free speech together and would reject the claim that wealth empties them, inferred from its principles.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Conservatism values established law and constitutional order against arbitrary rule, inferred from Burke and the platform's constitutionalism.

racial-franchise.rationale: The scope excludes the extreme right and racial supremacy, and the mainstream right supports equal citizenship in law.

online-participation.rationale: The right is divided on online participation; it is not a defining position of the label.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream right's support for limited, accountable government and scrutiny of bureaucracy.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Mainstream right-wing parties in democracies defend religious freedom, so they oppose legal limits on interfaith marriage, inferred from the platform.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The mainstream right opposes religious discrimination in the marketplace, inferred from the platform's defence of religious liberty.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The Burkean and centre-right tradition prefers elected representatives and established institutions to novel participatory devices, inferred from that stance rather than any stated position on assemblies.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious conservatives favor preserving inherited doctrine, while secular and liberal strands of the right are indifferent, so adherents are split.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The right defends property and unequal outcomes and sees wealth as a source of social order, though some strands share worry about concentrated power; inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The right is split between social conservatives and libertarian or centre-right strands on this question.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The right defends religion as a pillar of social order, as in Burke, and rejects state promotion of atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Law and order and strong policing are central to the mainstream right.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The right has no common position on consociational arrangements; inferred, adherents differ.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The right favours civil society, family and local communities over state programs, in the tradition of Burke's little platoons.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are popular on the populist and US right; inferred, not documented in the cited sources.

vote-delegation.rationale: Burke held that representatives exercise judgement and are not bound by instruction, so delegable voting runs against that tradition; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Existential risk is not tied to the right-left divide; inferred neutral.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Traditional and religious strands of the right resist this, though the centre-right is split; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Traditional strands favour male headship while the centre-right accepts shared authority, so adherents split.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The mainstream right ties the franchise to citizenship and national membership; inferred from its nation and tradition emphasis, though some centre-right parties accept local votes for long-term residents.

rent-control.rationale: Centre-right and US platform economics favour property rights and market supply as the remedy for housing shortages; inferred from that stance.

abolish-ip.rationale: The right's emphasis on property and enterprise makes legal protection of patents and copyright a settled position; inferred from its property principles.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The mainstream democratic right values voluntary civil society, family and tradition over state-run drilled youth movements, which belong to the excluded extreme right; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The mainstream right generally backs nuclear deterrence and alliance basing, so it rejects a ban on hosting; inferred from its security stance.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The mainstream right generally supports security alliances and allied basing, though national-conservative strands stress sovereignty; inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Adherents split: national-conservatives and many centre-right governments recognise genocides readily, while others leave it to historians or avoid diplomatic costs; no source settles it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The right defends returns on property and investment as legitimate and productive; inferred from Burke's defence of property.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The right strongly upholds self-defence and defence of others, and the Republican platform backs the right to bear arms and law and order.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Conservative and national-conservative thought values inherited national continuity, as Burke's idea of an inheritance across generations suggests, though adherents differ on antiquity; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The mainstream right treats sex as a biological fact and the 2024 Republican platform opposes gender-ideology claims, though it does not address the philosophical point directly.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The right sees women as a natural category and is generally hostile to identity-politics framings of feminism; inferred from its traditionalism.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring the fallen is common on the right, but sacred veneration as martyrs and saints is a religious-nationalist idea not shared by most secular conservatives; adherents split.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Religious conservatives and some US right figures frame politics as moral and spiritual conflict, while Burkean and centre-right adherents stress prudence and compromise; split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The label does not address diaspora and homeland roles; the question belongs to specific nationalisms and adherents have no common view.

culture-before-state.rationale: Burkean conservatives hold that institutions grow from custom, but national-conservatives stress state action; no common order of priority is documented.

god-not-male.rationale: Traditional religious language is generally kept by the religious and cultural right; the 2024 platform's traditionalist stance suggests this, inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Conservatives hold that religious tradition has authority as received, not subject to a feminist test; inferred from Burke's respect for inherited religion.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The mainstream right defends open markets and equal legal treatment, so it rejects ethnic allocation of economic life, though nationalist strands favour national preference; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not a concern of the mainstream right, which keeps existing administrative borders; inferred from its preference for established institutions.

notes: The strands diverge on trade, welfare, intervention, religion in public life and the role of the state: neoliberal, traditionalist and national-conservative answers differ, so those are 0 or low confidence. The US platform source reflects one national party and was used only for stated planks.
